statement.text:
A subgroup H of a group G is called pronormal if H and H g are conjugate in
⟨H, H g ⟩ for every g ∈ G. A subgroup H of a group G is called abnormal if g ∈ ⟨H, H g ⟩
for every g ∈ G.
    Does there exist an infinite group that does not contain nontrivial proper pronor-
mal subgroups?
    The question is equivalent to the following: does there exist an infinite simple
group that does not contain proper abnormal subgroups?                     D. O. Revin
  ∗ Yes, it does (S. Corson, Monatsh. Math. (2025) https://doi.org/10.1007/
s00605-025-02116-8.
